# Code of Conduct

This Code of Conduct sets expectations for everyone who participates in this
project. It is a template. Before adopting it, maintainers must replace the
reporting placeholders and confirm that the process matches their organisation's
policies.

## Our commitment

We aim to maintain a respectful, inclusive, and safe project community. We work
with professionalism, compassion, and openness, and treat people with dignity.
Where applicable, these aims reflect the values in the
[NHS Constitution for England](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-nhs-constitution-for-england/the-nhs-constitution-for-england#nhs-values).
They do not replace an organisation's employment policies, professional
standards, or statutory duties.

## Expected behaviour

- Treat everyone with respect, fairness, and consideration, regardless of role,
  seniority, identity, background, or level of experience.
- Be constructive when discussing technical decisions. Critique ideas and work,
  not people.
- Listen to different viewpoints, give and receive feedback in good faith, and
  take responsibility for the impact of your actions.
- Help make participation accessible. Be considerate of different communication
  styles, needs, and levels of experience.
- Credit other people's work and respect licences and confidentiality.
- Protect patient, personal, and confidential information. Use synthetic
  examples and approved channels when discussing sensitive matters.

## Unacceptable behaviour

Unacceptable behaviour includes:

- Harassment, bullying, discrimination, intimidation, threats, or abusive or
  degrading language.
- Personal attacks, unwanted sexual attention, or conduct that repeatedly
  ignores a clear request to stop.
- Sharing or seeking to expose another person's private information, patient
  information, credentials, or confidential material without authorisation.
- Impersonation, retaliation against someone who raises a concern in good faith,
  or deliberate disruption of project spaces.
- Knowingly making a malicious or fabricated report. A report is not misconduct
  simply because it cannot be substantiated.

## Scope

This policy applies to project spaces, including repositories, issues, pull
requests, code reviews, discussions, project-managed communication channels, and
project events. It also applies when someone is clearly acting as a
representative of the project in another setting.

This policy governs participation in the project community. It does not replace
NHS or employer processes for employment concerns, whistleblowing, safeguarding,
patient safety, clinical safety, information governance, data breaches, or
security incidents. Use the appropriate organisational route for those matters.

Do not report conduct concerns in public issues or pull requests. Do not include
patient-identifiable information or other sensitive details in a report unless
the approved route specifically requires them. Do not use this Code of Conduct
as a route for reporting security vulnerabilities. Follow
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) instead.

## How reports are handled

The designated contact will review reports as promptly as practicable and
explain the next steps. Reports will be handled sensitively. Information will be
shared only with people who need it to assess or respond, subject to legal,
safeguarding, and safety obligations. Absolute confidentiality cannot be
guaranteed.

The project will consider reports fairly and impartially. Anyone named in a
report will have an appropriate opportunity to respond. A person with a conflict
of interest must not decide the outcome. Where necessary, the alternate contact
or the relevant organisational process should handle the matter.

The project does not tolerate retaliation against someone who raises a concern
in good faith or participates in a review. If you believe retaliation has
occurred, report it through the same private route or its alternative.

## Possible outcomes

Maintainers or the designated organisation may take action proportionate to the
behaviour, its impact, and any relevant pattern. Actions may include a private
request to stop or correct behaviour, a warning, removal of content, temporary
restrictions, removal from project spaces, or referral to an appropriate
organisational process. Immediate protective action may be needed while a
concern is reviewed.

Where practicable, the person affected may ask for a review by someone not
involved in the original decision. Do not publish private report details or
enforcement discussions in project spaces.
